:::{#exm-matmul-product-of-sums}
#### Order matters in the expansion

Take $\matr{A} = \matr{C} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\matr{B} = \matr{D} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.
Then $\matr{A} + \matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$, so

$$
\ba
(\matr{A} + \matr{B})^2 &= \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5 \end{bmatrix}, \\
\matr{A}^2 + \matr{A}\matr{B} + \matr{B}\matr{A} + \matr{B}^2
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
+ \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
+ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}
+ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5 \end{bmatrix}.
\ea
$$

Here $\matr{A}\matr{B} \neq \matr{B}\matr{A}$, so the middle terms do not combine into $2\matr{A}\matr{B}$.
The squared norm of a sum of vectors, $\norm{\vx + \vy}^2$, is the one case where they do combine (@thm-norm-sum-square), because $\vx \cdot \vy = \vy \cdot \vx$.

:::
